hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the target's own aligned view (fnasm --diff, whole function) was read at BASELINE and after every probe; what has NOT been checked is whether the m-parameter copy can be made to precede the base materialization at all.
hypothesis.statement: The two remaining clusters are independent and only the first is still open. CLUSTER 1 (capped elsewhere): the target completes the global base address BEFORE the frame is set, defining it at `@0x10 addi r0,r8,0 @lbl_8011D568(ADDR16_LO)` - above `@0x14 stwu r1,-136(r1)` - while ours defines it at `@0x24 addi r5,r8,0 @lbl_8011D568(ADDR16_LO)`, below the prologue, because in our stream r5 still holds the `m` parameter until `@0x1c addi r26,r5,0` copies it away; the target sinks the value into r0, which `@0x8 stw r0,4(r1)` has just freed. The untried lever is therefore NOT another spelling of the base variable (the 2026-08-26 cap exhausted those) but any construct that stops r5 from being the natural home, e.g. giving the third parameter a copy-local of its own so the param registers are drained in a different order. CLUSTER 2 (closed by this record): the node-copy local is defined at `@0x20 addi r30,r7,0` in ours against `@0x24 addi r31,r7,0` in the target, and the arrH[].d load at `@0x58 lwz r31,548(r3)` in ours against `@0x58 lwz r30,548(r3)` in the target - a two-register trade that two declaration probes proved unreachable.
